current.text: He is projected as a bench player in Brooklyn's second unit. He competes with Julius Randle, Josh Minott and Danny Wolf for minutes at the four, in a crowded frontcourt.
Brooklyn did not give him a contract extension, so this is a pivotal season for him.
He is not a draft target. The experts say the Randle trade ended his fantasy value.
The second half of the season is uncertain for Brooklyn. The team could give more minutes to young players, Clowney among them, and Michael Porter Jr. could be traded.
Brooklyn is projected to be one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins. Houston owns its pick, so the Nets have no reason to tank. They are running a development season.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. In our playoff weeks 19 to 21 the Nets play 3, 4 and 3 games, with only one back-to-back.

durable.text: His shot is unreliable. He has not been an efficient three-point shooter so far, even though he has had hot stretches.
His production has been inconsistent, and so have his defensive stats and shot blocking. He needs to improve his rebounding and rim protection.
He has battled injuries in his career.

note: Do not draft him. Yahoo ranks him 234 and ESPN ranks him 269, both value him at 0 USD, and our auction takes only 144 players. He projects as a bench forward with a weak shot: 39.6% FG on 9.6 attempts last season, and neither site projects better than about 40% FG. Leave him on waivers and watch for a bigger role later in the season, if Brooklyn trades Porter or moves minutes to its young players.
